case.case_title: Dhammiaka Yapa v. Bandaranayake and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. 110/87, decided on 17 November 1987

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the arrest of Mahinda Wijesekera was lawful and whether he was informed of the reason for his arrest as required by Article 13(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that Wijesekera was arrested without lawful grounds and was not informed of the reason for his arrest.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the arrest was lawful based on a reasonable complaint by the Minister of Finance and that Wijesekera was informed of the reason for his arrest.
key_facts: Wijesekera was arrested on 30.7.87 by police officers acting on a telephone complaint from the Minister of Finance.
The complaint alleged Wijesekera led a mob that attacked the Minister's house.
Police had reasonable grounds to suspect Wijesekera of committing an offence under Emergency Regulations.
The 2nd respondent stated he informed Wijesekera of the reason for arrest in the presence of his wife.
Wijesekera, an attorney-at-law, would have asked and been told the reason for his arrest.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that arrest must be according to law and the arrested person must be informed of the reason. The complaint by the Minister was reasonable and credible, justifying the arrest. The police officer personally had reasonable suspicion and informed Wijesekera of the reason.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the Minister's complaint credible and the police officer justified in acting on it. The contemporaneous police notes and affidavits supported that Wijesekera was informed of the reason for arrest.
principles_established: Arrest without warrant is lawful if based on reasonable suspicion or complaint under law.
Police officers must personally have reasonable grounds for arrest, not merely act on orders.
Informing the arrested person of the reason is required and was satisfied here.

outcome.holding: The court held that Wijesekera's arrest was lawful and he was informed of the reason, thus no violation of Article 13(1).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) protects against unlawful arrest and requires informing the arrested person of the reason. The court's reasoning and outcome centrally depend on whether these requirements were met.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The 2nd respondent explained to Wijesekera in the presence of his wife the reason for arrest related to damage caused to the Minister's house; police notes and affidavits confirm this.
